note.label: Esau the Hater, Liar, and Killer

precepts.why:
Psalms 50:16 says “But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes”. Before reading on, identify the wicked: “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked”.

Let's examine it. Who is running the earth? Who has military bases all over the world? Whose money is the money you must do business with? The so-called white man, Esau. Who has the power to go into another country, take out its leader, bring him to their own country, and nothing happens to them? Who can say, I don't like your policies, we're going to kill you? They did it in Libya. Recently they did it in Haiti: they killed the president. He didn't want the COVID vaccine, and he had just come from a meeting in Turkey with Russian officials and struck a deal with Russia to make Haiti what it is supposed to be. Two months later: no, you've got to go. Look at the man's rap sheet: a murderer, a killer, and insatiable.

“he covereth the faces of the judges thereof”. Who are the judges? We are. And our faces are covered because we are not known. You can see it on the walls of those churches in Russia and Romania: you still have the black images we left behind. But when they paint a new picture, they paint it white. That is how they covered the faces of the judges. All their movies are white; go on Google and everything is white. But in the Bible, the judges are black.

So when God says to the wicked, what hast thou to do to declare my statutes, he is speaking to the one whose hand the earth was given into. As a Christian he declares the Lord's statutes, as a Jew he claims to keep the laws, taking the old covenant and the new, remixing them and saying everybody can be saved, while he covers the faces of the true judges and takes the land by wickedness.

note.label: Give Diligence

precepts.why:

They will never change as a race of people. That's why it has been a perpetual hatred from Cain to Abel, Jacob to Esau, blacks and whites, playing itself out over and over, while Christianity blinds us from accepting what God is telling us.

Not we-got-the-vote peace: you still get jailed, racially profiled, shot down, and you can't do what white people do when they get pulled over. As a result of all this enslavement and all these massacres, Esau is thinking a certain way now. He thinks he's getting away with it: “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence.” Oh, wait a minute, we just enslaved the Lord's people and he didn't do anything.

“thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself.” That is what Esau is thinking to this day. That's why they don't hold themselves accountable for anything. They hold themselves not guilty when they slay us, when they kill us, when they put us into slavery, when they don't give us reparations. Esau thinks he is God.

“but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.” There will be a judgment for these things. So don't think that smiling white man in your face means to do you good.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
The wicked of Psalms 50 hates instruction and casts God's words behind him, and “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.” Sirach shows the right way to deal with a brother or friend: “Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more.”

“Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again. Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.”

So why do we sit and speak against our brother? Because sometimes a brother admonishes you, and now you are angry behind it. Why are you mad? Why is it bothering you? Admonishing is what a friend is supposed to do. The one who hates instruction turns the admonishment around and slanders the brother who gave it.

God says to that man, “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee”. Just because he didn't do anything right away, don't think you are going to get away with it.

precepts.text: A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother. Friend and brother are synonymous in this teaching; the slander of Psalms 50:20 lands on both.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
Why is a friend's admonishment the same matter as speaking against your brother? Because friend and brother are synonymous. Proverbs explains it: “A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.”

There are some friends that are closer than a brother. So when Psalms 50:20 says “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son”, the slander lands on the friend who admonished you as much as on your own blood.

A man that has friends must show himself friendly, not turn on the friend who corrects him. And God will not keep silence forever: “Now consider this, ye that forget God, lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver.” That is Israel, because the other nations never knew God to forget him. “and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God”, and the salvation is only to Israel.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
This follows up on the saints: “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” Read the verse above it and see who is sent to do the gathering: “He shall call to the heavens from above, and to the earth, that he may judge his people.”

The heavens from above are the angels. The earth is the prophets. And what is the message to the angels and to the prophets? “Gather my saints together unto me.” So when the angels come, they are only gathering the saints. They are not gathering all races on the planet. They are only gathering the saints, the ones he judges as “his people.”

The angels and the prophets are only looking for Israelites, those that made a covenant with God by sacrifice. That is not all races on the planet. That is not the Philistines. That is not the Ishmaelites. That is not the Moabites. Only Israel.

So the saints that the mystery of Colossians 1:26 is made manifest to are the same saints the angels come to gather: the children of Israel, the people of the covenant.

precepts.text: He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints, even of the children of Israel. The children of Israel are the saints.
precepts.point: We are not supposed to be looking for other races and nationalities, only the twelve tribes of Israel.

note.label: Recovering the Remnant: Worldwide Blitz

precepts.why:
Christ said he would send his angels to gather the elect from the four winds, and Isaiah names the elect: “Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel mine elect.” The Israelites would not be in one land; they would be scattered worldwide. Before the angels come for them, the Lord says, “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” So who are the saints?

“He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel.” The children of Israel are the saints.

Now read Psalms 50 again with that. “He shall call to the heavens from above”: that is the angels he is calling to. “and to the earth”: the earth is you and I. And the message to both is the same, “Gather my saints together unto me.” That is what we read in Matthew 24, where Christ tells his angels to gather the elect, and it is the commandment to the prophets on earth too.

“those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice”: only the Israelites made a covenant with God by sacrifice. So we are not supposed to be looking for other races and other nationalities. The work of gathering is for the twelve tribes of Israel, the saints, scattered to the four corners of the earth.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Esau cried, “Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright; and, behold, now he hath taken away my blessing.” Is that true? Go back to Genesis 25. Esau came from the field faint and said, “Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage”. “And Jacob said, Sell me this day thy birthright.” There was no trickery. Jacob asked him straight, and it was up to Esau to say no. Esau said, “what profit shall this birthright do to me?” Jacob made him swear, because the word of that man is no good, just as with the four hundred and some treaties they broke. Scripture sums it up: “thus Esau despised his birthright.”

So Esau was lying and playing the victim. The Psalm describes it: “Thou givest thy mouth to evil, and thy tongue frameth deceit.” “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.” Did we not just read the slander? He tricked me two times. Nowhere does scripture show Jacob dealing with deceit over the birthright. They were liars from the beginning, because they moved in the same spirit as their father Cain, who was of the wicked one.

It is how they do today: throw the rock, hide the hand, and as soon as the other side hits back, run to the UN as the victim. Now all of a sudden he cares about the birthright, just as his children want to stand in our place claiming to be the Jews and the people of the book. Where was that energy when he threw it away for something to eat, or today for money and fame?

You got the children of God and you got the children of the devil; there is no in between. You either got the godly mind or the Edomite mind. The same Psalm says to the wicked, the white man, “What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” “Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.” They say in God we trust and swear on the Bible while doing nothing the scripture says.

Esau “lifted up his voice, and wept”, but that was worldly sorrow. “For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.” We must come to the Lord sincerely, because of those who wait, God says, “Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me:” “For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord”. “Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way”. We all have to examine ourselves so we are not moving in that same spirit.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
This is the Edomite mindset, the carnal mind at war with God. “But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” Unto the wicked, the white man, God says: hold on, you are carnally minded. Why are you out there talking about in God we trust? Why are you swearing in on the Bible when you do nothing according to the scriptures?

“Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.” He talks about in God we trust while he has transgenders out there, putting two men together. They don't do anything the scriptures say. They cast the word behind their back, because the carnal mind is at war with God.

This is the battle of the spirit and the flesh, and that inner battle is within us too. It is the same profane spirit Hebrews names in Esau, whose religion is sin and who despised what was sacred. So we have to make sure we stand in the spirit, and not take God's covenant in our mouth while we cast his words behind us, as a brother does when he holds on to a bitter spirit.

note.label: Edom: The Robbers of thy people revealed past and present

precepts.why:
Edom said of Israel's two nations, “shall be mine, and we will possess it”. David shows what the wicked did with that: “But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth? Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.”

“Thou givest thy mouth to evil, and thy tongue frameth deceit”: lies. “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.” Esau's own mother's son is Jacob: us. He speaks against us and says we are not God's people.

“These things hast thou done, and I kept silence”: I let you do it. But “thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself”: you thought I was white like you. They made the heavenly Father white, the angels white, Christ white, and made themselves gods over people. God says, I'm not you.

So the Lord says, “but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.” I will correct you, and as Ezekiel 37:10 shows, I will let you know that I am among my people. “Now consider this, ye that forget God, lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver.”

That is why Ezekiel says, “I have heard all thy blasphemies which thou hast spoken against the mountains of Israel, saying, They are laid desolate, they are given us to consume.” Laid desolate: we are enslaved. Given us to consume: consumed spiritually and literally, physically destroyed. And the blasphemy of Revelation 2:9 is “of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.”

precepts.text: Edom shall be called the border of wickedness and the people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.
precepts.point: What hast thou to do to take my covenant in thy mouth: one group of Esau took the new covenant as Christians and the land of America, the other took the old covenant in 1948 as Jews and the land of Israel, and both hate instruction and cast God's words behind them.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
“But unto the wicked God saith”. Who is the wicked? Malachi gives the name: “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places”. Edom is Esau, Mount Seir; it is the same subject.

But “thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” They shall call Edom the border of wickedness. And note it says the people, not the person. The apologists like to play word games and say it is talking about the person Esau. No: people is plural, meaning all of them. And how long is the Lord's indignation against them? For ever.

So the psalm is speaking to Edom: “What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” Esau said in Ezekiel 35:10, “These two nations and these two countries shall be mine”: the kingdoms of Judah and Israel, and the two countries America and Israel. They took America as Christians and the land of Israel as Jewish people.

One group of Esau took the new covenant as Christians and took the land. The other group, in 1948, took the old covenant and said, we are the Jews. Whether they call themselves Jewish or Christian, they hate instruction and cast God's words behind them. They are the wicked, the border of wickedness.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
Jeremiah says the Lord's device is against Babylon “to destroy it; because it is the vengeance of the Lord, the vengeance of his temple.” The Lord has not forgotten what the Romans did to our temple under Titus and Vespasian, and the Romans today are the United States of America, the same people. They thought that God forgot.

David shows it: “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself”. The Lord is patient and longsuffering. Because he kept silence, they thought he forgot what they did to our temple, as if he were like them.

Then: “but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.” The Lord will reprove them, and that is what he is doing in these last days: setting things in order before their eyes, and there is nothing they can do about it.

That is why “the Lord hath raised up the spirit of the kings of the Medes”, the Iranians. The Lord put this mindset in them, always to be against Babylon, the United States of America. “Make bright the arrows; gather the shields”: those arrows are the ICBMs, the nukes, the bombs. They are not scared and they are not backing down, because the vengeance of his temple has not been forgotten.

precepts.point: The power is in keeping the commandments and the faith of Christ; then God and his angels fight for his people.

note.label: Latinos For Trump: Alien Vs. Predator

precepts.why:
“Servants have ruled over us: there is none that doth deliver us out of their hand.” Esau knows who he is and knows this is his time to rule, but it is coming to an end: servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth. None can deliver us. Hugo Chavez could not do it. Fidel Castro could not do it. Maduro could not do it, even with Russian helicopters and Chinese spyware. The 32 Cuban bodyguards around Maduro went back to Cuba in little boxes, mini coffins draped with the Cuban flag. A head of state snatched out of his fortress in three hours or less, with no casualties on the American side.

So we cannot expect a man to save us from this wicked, demonic people. The small groups picking up arms against them are agitation, agents provocateurs setting us up for failure. Where do you get your bullets? You have no factories. You would have to go to your enemy for the weapons to use against him. Our power is keeping God's commandments and the faith of Christ; then the Most High and his angels fight for us.

The Lord speaks to Esau: “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence.” These things: destroying my people, putting yokes of iron on their necks, having them hate themselves and their people. He says, “thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself.” Because God did not bring swift judgment, since he was punishing us for our iniquities, Esau thought God was with him, thought God looked like him. No, Esau. God is a black God. Jesus Christ is a black God.

Then: “but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.” The Most High will reprove Esau for the evil he has done to our people, and set Israel in order before his eyes.
